history.heading: Duklja and Zeta
paragraphs: The region of Montenegro was inhabited by Illyrians and later part of the Roman and Byzantine empires. Slavs settled in the 7th century. The medieval principality of Duklja and later Zeta emerged. Venice controlled coastal towns such as Kotor, whose bay and fortifications are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

history.heading: Independent mountain state
paragraphs: As the Ottomans conquered the Balkans, the mountainous core of Montenegro kept effective autonomy. From 1696 it was ruled by prince-bishops of the Petrović-Njegoš dynasty; Petar II Petrović-Njegoš wrote the epic The Mountain Wreath. Montenegro's independence was internationally recognised at the Congress of Berlin in 1878, and it became a kingdom in 1910.

history.heading: Yugoslavia and independence
paragraphs: After the First World War Montenegro was absorbed into the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes. It was a republic within socialist Yugoslavia and later formed a federation with Serbia. In a 2006 referendum, Montenegrins narrowly voted for independence. Montenegro joined NATO in 2017 and is considered the frontrunner to join the EU.

culture.heading: Language and identity
paragraphs: Montenegrin is the official language, closely related to Serbian; Serbian, Bosnian, Albanian and Croatian are also used. Most people are Orthodox Christian, with Muslim and Catholic minorities. National identity is divided between those who identify as Montenegrins and those who identify as Serbs.
The Ostrog Monastery, built into a cliff, is a major pilgrimage site. Njeguški pršut (smoked ham) and cheese are specialities. Water polo is the most successful sport.

politics.heading: Parliamentary republic
paragraphs: Montenegro is a parliamentary republic. Milo Đukanović and his party dominated politics for three decades until 2020. Since then, coalition governments have included pro-Western and pro-Serbian parties. EU accession reforms on corruption and rule of law are a top priority.

economy.heading: Tourism economy
paragraphs: Tourism on the Adriatic coast, such as Budva and the Bay of Kotor, and in the mountains is the main industry. Energy, aluminium and agriculture also contribute. Montenegro uses the euro, though not as an official eurozone member. A large highway built by a Chinese company created significant debt.
